title: Five correlated subqueries in the SELECT list
prompt: Monthly export, usually @Channel = 'Web' for one month (about 230k orders). It runs about 4.5 minutes. Plan: five
outer-join branches. OrderLines is read twice and Payments three times, each Payments access through
IX_Payments_OrderID and a Key Lookup. The consumer is a finance CSV that distinguishes NULL from 0: an order with no
lines must show LineCount 0 and Units empty (NULL). An order with no settled payment shows SettledAmount, LastPaidAt
and LastMethod empty. Orders with several payments and orders with several lines are both common.
data_notes: Azure SQL Database, General Purpose Gen5, 8 vCores, compatibility level 160. READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON. Query Store READ_WRITE. Collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. All foreign keys are trusted. Statistics: auto create and auto update ON; a nightly job updates Orders, OrderLines and Payments with FULLSCAN.

Orders: 30M rows, 2016 to now, ~12k per day now. The 25 partner customers own ~9M orders (30%), up to 1.2M each. Other customers average ~10 orders (max ~400). The density estimate for CustomerID is ~15 rows. Status: Shipped 83.8%, Cancelled 7%, Paid 6%, Returned 3%, Pending 0.2% (~60k rows, all from the last 72 hours). SalesChannel: Web 62%, Store 20%, Partner 12%, Phone 6%. PromoCode is NULL for 85%. ShipRegionID is NULL for Store pickups (~20%). OrderDate is datetime2(7); Partner and Store imports stamp one timestamp on a whole batch, so many orders of one customer share an OrderDate.
OrderLines: 120M rows, 4 per order on average. About 0.3% of orders have no lines.

Payments: 60M rows. Status: Settled 88%, Failed 6%, Refunded 4% (negative Amount), Pending 2%. ExternalRef is NULL for ~30%; non-NULL values are almost unique, with a few duplicates from provider retries. Partner accounts have up to 180k Settled or Refunded payments each. Settlement batches stamp the same PaidAt on 50-500 payments.
baseline_sql: (SELECT COUNT(*)         FROM qe.OrderLines ol WHERE ol.OrderID = o.OrderID)                        AS LineCount,
(SELECT SUM(ol.Quantity) FROM qe.OrderLines ol WHERE ol.OrderID = o.OrderID)                        AS Units,
(SELECT SUM(p.Amount)    FROM qe.Payments p WHERE p.OrderID = o.OrderID AND p.Status = 'Settled')   AS SettledAmount,
(SELECT MAX(p.PaidAt)    FROM qe.Payments p WHERE p.OrderID = o.OrderID AND p.Status = 'Settled')   AS LastPaidAt,
WHERE p.OrderID = o.OrderID AND p.Status = 'Settled' ORDER BY p.PaidAt DESC)                      AS LastMethod

correct_families.description: One scalar-aggregate APPLY per source table, and the last settled payment taken from one row.
reference_sql: lp.PaidAt AS LastPaidAt, lp.PaymentMethod AS LastMethod
CROSS APPLY (SELECT COUNT(*) AS LineCount, SUM(ol.Quantity) AS Units
WHERE p.OrderID = o.OrderID AND p.Status = 'Settled') pa
ORDER BY p.PaidAt DESC, p.PaymentID DESC) lp

traps.why: One join to both OrderLines and Payments multiplies the rows: Units is multiplied by the payment count and SettledAmount by the line count.
traps.told_apart_by: An order with two lines and two settled payments.
example_sql: COUNT(ol.LineNumber) AS LineCount, SUM(ol.Quantity) AS Units,
SUM(p.Amount) AS SettledAmount, MAX(p.PaidAt) AS LastPaidAt, MAX(p.PaymentMethod) AS LastMethod
LEFT JOIN qe.OrderLines ol ON ol.OrderID = o.OrderID
LEFT JOIN qe.Payments p ON p.OrderID = o.OrderID AND p.Status = 'Settled'
GROUP BY o.OrderID, o.OrderDate, o.Status, o.TotalAmount;

traps.why: The consumer distinguishes NULL from 0. ISNULL on Units or SettledAmount turns 'no lines' and 'no settled payment' into 0.
traps.told_apart_by: An order with no lines, or an order with no settled payment.
example_sql: lp.PaidAt AS LastPaidAt, lp.PaymentMethod AS LastMethod
CROSS APPLY (SELECT COUNT(*) AS LineCount, ISNULL(SUM(ol.Quantity), 0) AS Units
WHERE p.OrderID = o.OrderID AND p.Status = 'Settled') pa
ORDER BY p.PaidAt DESC, p.PaymentID DESC) lp

traps.why: CROSS APPLY on the TOP (1) branch returns no row for an order that has no settled payment.
traps.told_apart_by: An order with no settled payment.
example_sql: lp.PaidAt AS LastPaidAt, lp.PaymentMethod AS LastMethod
CROSS APPLY (SELECT COUNT(*) AS LineCount, SUM(ol.Quantity) AS Units
WHERE p.OrderID = o.OrderID AND p.Status = 'Settled') pa
ORDER BY p.PaidAt DESC, p.PaymentID DESC) lp

traps.why: MAX(PaymentMethod) is the alphabetically last method, not the method of the latest payment.
traps.told_apart_by: An order settled first by PayPal and later by Card.
example_sql: CROSS APPLY (SELECT COUNT(*) AS LineCount, SUM(ol.Quantity) AS Units
FROM qe.OrderLines ol WHERE ol.OrderID = o.OrderID) l
CROSS APPLY (SELECT SUM(p.Amount) AS SettledAmount, MAX(p.PaidAt) AS LastPaidAt, MAX(p.PaymentMethod) AS LastMethod
FROM qe.Payments p WHERE p.OrderID = o.OrderID AND p.Status = 'Settled') pa

min_improvement.basis: OrderLines goes from two accesses to one, Payments from three to two or one, and the key lookups go.

key.reference_notes: A single Payments access with ROW_NUMBER or MAX(CASE ...) is also exact and cheaper than two accesses.
